title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with launches and funding, as satellite constellations proliferate and new partnerships form. Meanwhile, the budget for space resilience is getting a boost, even as some hypersonic tests continue to stall.

themes.title: Launches and Satellite Deployments
themes.body: Ariane 6 is gearing up to deliver 36 Amazon Leo satellites, showcasing the growing reliance on upgraded boosters. Meanwhile, the Qianfan constellation has reached 200 satellites, confirming that the race for LEO supremacy is well underway.

themes.title: Funding and Valuations
themes.body: Apex's valuation has soared to $2.3 billion following a $200 million funding round, indicating strong investor confidence in satellite manufacturing. True Anomaly also raised $190 million, suggesting that the appetite for space startups remains robust.

themes.title: Defense and Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup has added $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, reflecting a growing recognition of the need for robust defense capabilities in orbit. This comes as Anduril and L3Harris team up for a tactical SDA constellation bid, signaling increased collaboration in the defense sector.

themes.title: Challenges in Hypersonics
themes.body: The hypersonic glide-vehicle test has slipped again, marking the third consecutive quarter of delays. This raises questions about the pace of advancements in a field that many see as critical for future military capabilities.
